newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ISPAT'S NEW ADR TRADES HIGHER.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ISPAT'S NEW ADR TRADES HIGHER.

text.p: Dutch steel group Ispat International was trading in heavy volume after making its first issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADR) on Thursday, dealers said.
"It's definitely the most active," said one trader, referring to European ADRs.
He said the group's initial public offering or IPO would receive special attention from investors for a few more days, given its novelty.
Ispat's ADR was at 39-3/16, up from a pricing of about $27.
The dealer said about nine million ADRs had changed hands in morning trading. A total of 25 million were offered.
Each ADR is equal to one share in the group.
Among other European ADRs, Royal Dutch Petroleum was 1-9/16 lower at 55-13/16 following the release of what one trader described as "disappointing" second-quarter results.
Royal Dutch/Shell Group had current cost income excluding special items of 1.140 billion sterling, a figure which fell in disfavor with investors.
In Latin America, Telecom Argentina SA was up 1/8 at 59-1/8 after reporting a net income of $75 million for the third quarter against $64 million for the same quarter a year ago.
The telecommunications company also announced it was adjusting its American Depositary Shares (ADSs) ratio to five share per ADS from 10 shares as of August 21.
"Anything to reduce the price is good news," said one dealer. "It will make it more liquid."

He said he was pleasantly surprised by the earnings, saying they showed how Telecom was performing better than the other Argentinian telecommunications company, Telefonica de Argentina, which was down 3/8 at 39-3/4.
Telebras SA was up 3/8 at 143-3/4 and Telefonos de Mexico was off 2/16 at 55-7/16.
Advancers led decliners 277 to 241 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group rose 0.31 percent and volume was 46.8 million ADRs.
ADRs enable the trade of foreign stock in the United States.
